address: Westerdok 536 / Westerdoksdijk 265-267, Amsterdam (Westerdokseiland): 2008 brick apartment block around courtyards, stepped to 34 m
notes: Westerdok 536 / Westerdoksdijk 265-267 (BAG), built 2008: a courtyard block on Westerdokseiland, brick base of about 10 m with set-back 34 m towers (tall narrow windows on the south front, w03-185 2022-04-21; stacked cantilevered balconies and a glazed ground floor on the west front, w01-275 2024-11-21; curved east front of grey-brown brick with ribbon balcony bands, w04-104; perforated-brick screens and loggias on the north, w02-5).

Modelled: brick-bay-grid with narrow windows (no frame rings, no sills, to fit 12k) on the S, W and N base fronts (3 storeys under the 10.4 m eaves), a 9-storey group on the 34 m tower walls (4 bays, courtyard walls included), and a 6-storey group on the curved east front (facets share one group). Simplified: the cantilevered dark balcony stacks on the west front, the perforated-brick screens and the loggia bays are plain punched windows; the glazed ground floor is a window row.

Known gate false negative: the BAG LoD0 footprint is the outer ring (10,004 m2) while 3DBAG LoD2.2 has a 3,755 m2 courtyard void, so footprint-vs-bag is 0.624 (needs >= 0.90). Every other gate passes. Not installable until the gate accepts a BAG footprint that spans a LoD2.2 courtyard.

Components lane (2026-10-13): the curved east front (walls[3], w04-104) is one curved run of 11 linked 3DBAG facets (65 m, 18 degrees; runs.ts) with curve: true, so its bay rhythm continues round the curve at one window width instead of restarting on every facet (facets of 4-8 m had one window each, sized to the facet). The run keeps the group pitch (11 bays); the straight panel 254 keeps its own 8 bays.
